title: Godot's physical light unit luminance seems to be different from Blender and Unreal Engine
body: ### Tested versions - Reproduced in Godot 4.7.1 stable ### System information Godot v4.7.1.stable - macOS Sequoia (15.7.1) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M2 Max (Apple8) - Apple M2 Max (12 threads) - 64.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description When using a Directional Light with a HDRI with absolute luminance value at 1000 cd/m2 per unit luminance, the estimated Directional Light intensity need to be multiplied by 30, to match any Blender or UE render using a directional light with estimated Directional Light intensity / 1000. See these images: - Godot render of a directional light at estimated lux * 30, using internal buffer output, so no additional transform is applied. - Blender render of a directional light at estimated lux / 1000 under Cycles and EEVEE, using raw output, so no additional transform is applied. - Godot render of a directional light at estimated lux * 30, using normal output with linear tonemap and fixed 1.0 exposure multiplier, so only display transform is applied. - Blender render of a directional light at estimated lux / 1000 with Cycles and EEVEE, using standard view with fixed 0 exposure, so only display transform is applied. I can't exactly explain this problem, except for the fact that default background intensity is set at 30,000 nit, so my guess is Godot's physical unit luminance is somehow 30,000 times smaller than Blender and Unreal Engine. ### Steps to reproduce Open the Godot Project and compared the rendering result with Blender Project. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [godot-hdr-example.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30619834/godot-hdr-example.zip) [hdri-test4.blend.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30619837/hdri-test4.blend.zip) I removed the HDRI to keep the file size small (they are not needed to demonstrate the issue) Sunlight measurement were taken from this example (the lighting data csv is included in the example Godot project): https://www.bandainamcostudios.com/projects/truehdri/library/16888 For more info about why we use absolute HDRI: https://blog.selfshadow.com/publications/s2016-shading-course/unity/s2016_pbs_unity_hdri.pdf
